messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
The “standard deviation” you’re looking for is really the **standard error of the sample mean** under the null hypothesis.  
It’s calculated as:

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

where  
- \(s = 1.4\) (sample standard deviation)  
- \(n = 40\) (sample size)

\[
SE = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.2215
\]

So the standard error (i.e., the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean) is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user says: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That might refer to the standard error of the mean under null? Usually standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard error of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null. That would be sigma/sqrt(n). But we don't know population sigma; we have sample sigma 1.4. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. So answer ~0.2215.

But maybe they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? For t-test, t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(n)). The denominator is standard error. So standard deviation of test statistic is 1? Actually t distribution has variance n-1/(n-3) etc. But maybe they want the standard error.

Thus answer: 0.2215.

We can compute precisely: sqrt(40)=6.3249. 1.4/6.3249=0.2215.

Thus answer: about 0.2215.

We can also mention that this is the standard error of the mean. Provide explanation.

We don't need to call function. The function calculates p-value, not needed. So just answer.
